_meta.indication: Add-on maintenance treatment of patients with severe asthma aged 12 years and older, and with an eosinophilic phenotype.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled exacerbation trial, 48 weeks in duration.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥12 years with severe asthma on high-dose ICS plus LABA, with a history of 2 or more exacerbations in the past 12 months and ACQ-6 score of 1.5 or more.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Rate of asthma exacerbations in patients with baseline blood eosinophil counts ≥300 cells/µL taking high-dose ICS and LABA.
pivotal_trials.n: N=1204 (recommended-regimen primary population n=267 FASENRA, n=267 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Annual exacerbation rate 0.74 for FASENRA (30 mg every 8 weeks) vs 1.52 placebo; rate ratio 0.49 (95% CI 0.37, 0.64).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled exacerbation trial, 56 weeks in duration.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥12 years with severe asthma on medium or high dose ICS plus LABA, with a history of 2 or more exacerbations in the past 12 months and ACQ-6 score of 1.5 or more.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Rate of asthma exacerbations in patients with baseline blood eosinophil counts ≥300 cells/µL taking high-dose ICS and LABA.
pivotal_trials.n: N=1306 (recommended-regimen primary population n=239 FASENRA, n=248 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Annual exacerbation rate 0.73 for FASENRA (30 mg every 8 weeks) vs 1.01 placebo; rate ratio 0.72 (95% CI 0.54, 0.95).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, oral corticosteroid reduction trial with an 8-week OCS titration run-in.
pivotal_trials.population: Asthma patients requiring daily OCS (7.5 to 40 mg/day) plus high-dose ICS and LABA, with blood eosinophil counts ≥150 cells/µL and at least one exacerbation in the past 12 months.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent reduction from baseline of the final OCS dose during Weeks 24 to 28 while maintaining asthma control.
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent reduction in daily OCS dose from baseline was 75% for FASENRA (95% CI: 60, 88) vs 25% for placebo (95% CI: 0, 33).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%) are headache (8% vs 6% placebo) and pharyngitis (5% vs 3% placebo). Hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis, angioedema, urticaria, rash) have occurred.
target_moa: Benralizumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody (IgG1/kappa) selective for the interleukin-5 receptor alpha subunit (IL-5Rα), expressed on eosinophils and basophils; its afucosylated Fc domain binds FcγRIII on NK cells to induce apoptosis of eosinophils and basophils via antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC).

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class.

description.text: Expanded to add-on maintenance treatment of patients aged 6 to 11 years with severe asthma and an eosinophilic phenotype

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for updates to the indication statement for FASENRA, to include the use of FASENRA as add-on maintenance treatment of patients aged 6 to 11 years with severe asthma, and with an eosinophilic phenotype.

description.text: Added indication for treatment of adult patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for the use of Fasenra (benralizumab) injection for the treatment of adult patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

description.text: Added indication for treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES) without an identifiable non-hematologic secondary cause

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for addition of the indication for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES) without an identifiable non-hematologic secondary cause.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Standard (not Priority) review classification.

summary.text: FASENRA (benralizumab) was approved November 14, 2017 as a traditional (non-accelerated) approval under a Standard review BLA received November 16, 2016, based on three phase 3 trials (SIROCCO, CALIMA, ZONDA). The application was not referred to an advisory committee because the biologic is not the first in its class.

citations.quote:
Priority or Standard	Standard
